policy_title: Boost Sports Participation and Invest in Grassroots Facilities
stated: Boost participation in sports and physical activity by investing in leisure centres, swimming pools and other grassroots facilities and supporting community sports clubs.

source.quote: Boost participation in sports and physical activity by investing in leisure centres, swimming pools and other grassroots facilities and supporting community sports clubs.

bearing_set.reason: Increased population-level physical activity through accessible facilities has a documented preventive-health mechanism — reducing incidence of cardiovascular disease, obesity, diabetes, and poor mental health — that plausibly reduces NHS demand and affects waiting-list and mental-health-access indicators over time.

Community sports clubs are a primary site of social trust, volunteering, inter-group contact, and civic participation; explicitly funding them moves the indicators for belonging and social cohesion non-negligibly.

Capital investment in leisure centres and swimming pools plus revenue support for community clubs constitutes a material public spending commitment that affects the funded/borrowed balance and the debt path, regardless of any longer-run health-cost offsets (which are projected, not measured).

membership_note: Primary bearings are healthcare (O3) via the physical-activity–disease link, community cohesion (O15) via explicit support for community clubs, and public finances (O12) as the fiscal cost of the investment programme. Effects on inequality (O14) and prosperity (O13) exist but are too indirect and diffuse to clear the non-negligible bar on their own indicators.
